description: A bank of sixteen oscillator pairs tuned to a scale, spread apart in pitch and shaped by two waveshapers, mixed down to two outputs

params.text: Chooses which of ten scales the oscillators are tuned to
Spreads the oscillators apart in pitch, from all of them on the root to a wide chord
Sets the pitch of the whole bank
Sets how the level falls away across the bank, from the lowest oscillator pair to the highest
Sets the root note the scale and the spread are built from
Sets how much the oscillators frequency-modulate one another
Sets how hard the shaper chosen by the twist switch acts on the oscillators
Detunes the oscillators from each other
Sets how hard the shaper chosen by the warp switch acts on the oscillators' output
Chooses the grid the pitches are held to: FREE leaves them where they fall, OCT. holds them to octaves, and 12TET holds them to twelve-tone equal temperament
Chooses which way the cross modulation runs: UP has the first oscillator modulate all the rest, DOWN has the last one modulate them, and ALL chains each oscillator into the next
Chooses which of three shapers the TWIST knob drives: RAMP, PULSAR or CRUSH
Chooses which of three shapers the WARP knob drives: FOLD folds the wave back on itself, CHEB runs it through Chebyshev polynomials, and SEGMENT reads it from a table of triangle segments
Press it to start building a new scale and press it again to keep it; a long press throws away the scale being built
Press and release it to freeze part of the bank, so those oscillators hold what they are doing; while a new scale is being built, this removes the last note added instead

inputs.text: Moves the pitch of the whole bank, one octave per volt
Moves the root note, one octave per volt
Moves the SCALE setting; the voltage is read upside down, so -5V goes one way along the list and +5V the other
Moves the SPREAD knob; the voltage is read upside down, so -5V spreads the oscillators wider and +5V narrower
Moves the CROSS FM knob; the voltage is read upside down, so -5V raises it and +5V lowers it
While a new scale is being built, a rising edge above 1.5V adds the note at the PITCH jack to it
Moves the BALANCE knob; the voltage is read upside down, so -5V goes one way across the bank and +5V the other
Moves the TWIST knob; the voltage is read upside down, so -5V raises it and +5V lowers it
Moves the WARP knob; the voltage is read upside down, so -5V raises it and +5V lowers it
Every edge above 1.5V, rising or falling, turns freeze on or off

outputs.text: One side of the bank, the oscillators being split between the two outputs as the menu's StereoSplit setting says, about 9V peak

notes: The number of voices follows whichever of the two 1V/octave jacks has the most channels, up to four, and the sixteen oscillator pairs are shared out between them.
To build a scale: press LEARN, then send an edge to the LEARN jack for each note, with that note's pitch at the PITCH jack, and press LEARN again to keep it.
menu: FreezeSplit: Even/Odd, Low/High, Root/Others — chooses which oscillators the freeze holds
StereoSplit: Even/Odd, Low/High, Root/Others — chooses how the oscillators are split between the two outputs
Crossfade — blends the two output halves back into each other, so a setting in the middle sends some of each side to both jacks
NumOsc — sets how many oscillator pairs each voice runs, from one to sixteen
FineTune — trims the pitch of the whole bank

inputs.5: high above 1.5V · stepped · one channel only
